decision_conditions: The proposed change of use from a C3 dwelling to a C2 children's residential care home would result in the loss of an existing self-contained family home. The applicant has not provided sufficient evidence of a specific, localised need for additional C2 accommodation in West Drayton, including an audit of existing facilities or assessment of alternative sites.  As such, the proposal is contrary to Policies DMH 8 and DMHB 11 of the Hillingdon Local Plan: Part 2 - Development Management Policies (2020), Policy H12 of the London Plan (2021), and the National Planning Policy Framework (2024).

The submitted drawings do not demonstrate a functional or safe internal layout capable of supporting a children's residential care use. In particular, no communal living space, dining space, staff office/confidential space, staff bathroom or sleep-in staff bedroom is provided, despite the submitted management plan stating that sleep-in/waking night staff would be present. These omissions fail to provide a high quality internal environment and conflict with the expectations of the Children's Homes (England) Regulations 2015 and the statutory Guide to the Children's Homes Regulations including the Quality Standards (April 2015), which require premises to be designed and furnished to meet children's needs and enable participation in the daily life of the home. The development therefore fails to demonstrate acceptable living standards for future occupiers, contrary to NPPF (2024) paragraphs 130 and 135, London Plan (2021) Policy D6 and H12, and Hillingdon Local Plan Part 2 (2020) Policy DM

The proposed development fails to demonstrate that it can operate without causing unacceptable parking stress or adverse highway impacts, as the submitted Travel Management Plan contains material inaccuracies regarding on-site parking, cycle storage, and vehicle use. In the absence of accurate information the development at present would likely displace staff, visitor and operational parking onto surrounding residential streets which would intensify existing parking pressure and reduce the availability of spaces for local residents. The absence of accurate transport information, enforceable travel arrangements, and compliant cycle parking fails to comply with Policies DMT 1, DMT 2, DMT 5 and DMT 6 of the contrary to the minimum requirements of Hillingdon Local Plan Part 2 and Policies T5, and T6 of the London Plan (2021).

The application documents (including the Children's Home Management Plan and TMP) are inconsistent with the submitted plans and contain errors and assertions that are not physically deliverable on site. In the absence of accurate, coordinated information, the Local Planning Authority is unable to conclude that the proposal would provide a policy compliant standard of accommodation, protect neighbouring amenity or operate without undue highway/parking impact. The application therefore fails to meet the requirements of NPPF (2024) paragraph 135 and conflicts with the relevant provisions of the London Plan (2021) and Hillingdon Local Plan Part 2 (2020).

In dealing with the application the Council has implemented the requirement in the National Planning Policy Framework to work with the applicant in a positive and proactive way. We have made available detailed advice in the form of our statutory policies from the  Local Plan Part 1, Local Plan Part 2, Supplementary Planning Documents, Planning Briefs and other informal written guidance, as well as offering a full pre-application advice service.
description: Change of use from Class C3 (Dwellinghouse) to Class C2 (Residential Care Home), to include the conversion of roof space to habitable use including a rear dormer and front facing roof lights (Part retrospective application).
